EDUCATION.basis: a year of 'optional' school fees (1960s dollars)

EDUCATION.front: New books for your school: the other high school sent over its old set.
EDUCATION.red: The books are years out of date, marked up, with pages missing.
EDUCATION.amber: Your child studies from them until the other school gets new ones again.
EDUCATION.blue: The budget buys new books across town and passes the old ones down.
EDUCATION.basis: a year of books your child should have had (1960s dollars)

EDUCATION.front: The business school downtown: typing and shorthand, a career in six months.
EDUCATION.red: Tuition costs more than a year at a public college, for six months of classes.
EDUCATION.amber: Enroll by Monday or the price goes up, and the tuition isn't refunded if you quit.
EDUCATION.blue: The school is paid up front whether or not anyone hires its graduates.
EDUCATION.basis: private business-school tuition (1960s dollars)

EDUCATION.front: Finish your diploma by mail, and pay just a little per lesson.
EDUCATION.red: The lessons add up to far more than night classes at the high school.
EDUCATION.amber: Miss a payment and the lessons stop, but the balance is still due.
EDUCATION.blue: Many employers and colleges won't accept a mail-order diploma.
EDUCATION.basis: a year of mail-order lessons (1960s dollars)

EDUCATION.front: Freedom of choice: any family can now pick any school in the district.
EDUCATION.red: Transferring is free; just fill out the form.
EDUCATION.amber: The form is due by Friday, at the office during work hours, or your child is assigned back.
EDUCATION.blue: Plans like this kept schools segregated; the Supreme Court struck one down in 1968.
EDUCATION.basis: a year of the spending gap between schools (1960s dollars)

EDUCATION.front: The vocational track: your son will learn a trade and be working at eighteen.
EDUCATION.red: No fees, and the shop classes are real classes.
EDUCATION.amber: Once he's on the track he gets no college-prep courses; switching later means starting over.
EDUCATION.blue: Counselors steered Black students away from college before anyone asked them.
EDUCATION.basis: a year of the earnings gap from a closed path to college (1960s dollars)

EDUCATION.front: Cousins down South write: to register, just fill out the clerk's application.
EDUCATION.red: There is no charge to apply, and the clerk says anyone may try.
EDUCATION.amber: The clerk grades it on the spot and says when you may try again, months from now.
EDUCATION.blue: Southern states wrote those tests so the clerk could say no; the Voting Rights Act (1965) ended them.
EDUCATION.basis: a day's pay lost to the clerk's office (1960s dollars)

EDUCATION.front: A scholarship from the downtown club: full tuition, if you keep your grades up.
EDUCATION.red: It covers the whole first term, with nothing to pay back.
EDUCATION.amber: The club renews it term by term, on its own say, and can drop you mid-year.
EDUCATION.blue: The club decides what counts as 'keeping your grades up,' and can change it.
EDUCATION.basis: a year's tuition lost mid-year (1960s dollars)

EDUCATION.front: The school board wants a West Side parent on its new advisory committee.
EDUCATION.red: It costs nothing, and your name is in the paper.
EDUCATION.amber: It meets once a month, for a two-year term.
EDUCATION.blue: The committee has no vote, and the seat goes to the parent leading the school boycott.
EDUCATION.basis: a committee seat with no vote, for a year (1960s dollars)

EDUCATION.front: The district has a principal's job for you, starting in the fall.
EDUCATION.red: A real salary, a pension, and the respect of the title.
EDUCATION.amber: A one-year contract to start, renewed each spring.
EDUCATION.blue: It goes to the teacher who started the freedom school, if the freedom school closes.
EDUCATION.basis: a year of a principal's salary (1960s dollars)

EDUCATION.front: A full scholarship for your daughter at a college out of state, all expenses paid.
EDUCATION.red: Tuition, room and board, and a train ticket home at Christmas.
EDUCATION.amber: It starts this fall and renews every year she's in good standing.
EDUCATION.blue: It comes from the people your family is suing, if the family drops the case.
EDUCATION.basis: a year of college costs (1960s dollars)

EDUCATION.front: Central State University, near Xenia: low tuition, real aid, and teachers who expect you to finish.
EDUCATION.red: Public tuition, and a federal student loan at a low rate.
EDUCATION.amber: Repayment starts after you leave school, and part is forgiven if you teach.
EDUCATION.blue: A Black public university, built by and for the community it serves.
EDUCATION.basis: a year of low tuition and a federal student loan (1960s dollars)

EDUCATION.front: A citizenship class at the church: learn the forms and the ballot, then register together.
EDUCATION.red: Free, taught by neighbors at night, after work.
EDUCATION.amber: Classes run until the deadline, and the group goes down to register together.
EDUCATION.blue: Run by the community, for nobody's profit but the vote's.
EDUCATION.basis: a day's pay kept: the class meets after work (1960s dollars)

EDUCATION.front: The freedom school at the church: real classes while the boycott goes on.
EDUCATION.red: Free: volunteer teachers, donated books, lunch for every child.
EDUCATION.amber: It runs every school day of the boycott, so nobody falls behind.
EDUCATION.blue: The parents, the churches and the teachers who stand with them.
EDUCATION.basis: a boycott's worth of free classes and lunches (1960s dollars)

decision.text: Run for office, or keep organizing?

options.label: Run for office

options.label: Keep organizing

PLANTS_CLOSE.title: The Plants Close
PLANTS_CLOSE.intro: GM's Moraine plant closes in 2008; NCR leaves in 2009. Before the crash, the brokers came door to door with teaser rates and cash-out refinances. Now the temp agency is the only one hiring.
PLANTS_CLOSE.twist: Labor starts at Squeeze 2 and everyone starts with 1 Trust. Before the chapter the family chooses: defend what you built (the Machine strikes your Rebuilt districts first) or let one go (remove one Rebuilt sticker).
PLANTS_CLOSE.face_text: The Algorithm: scoring, automation and risk models. Relentless: the Machine strikes one extra time every round.

HOUSING.front: Refinance today and cut your payment way down! (2/28 loan)
HOUSING.red: Two years at a teaser rate, then it adjusts every six months, and the payment climbs by hundreds.
HOUSING.amber: The reset lands in month 25, and the prepayment penalty is built to outlast your chance to get out.
HOUSING.blue: The lender sells the loan upstream within weeks, so whether you can pay is someone else's problem.
HOUSING.basis: a payment about $300 a month higher after the reset, for a year (2000s dollars)

HOUSING.front: Cash out your equity: pay off the cards and fix the kitchen too!
HOUSING.red: Card debt becomes debt on your house, with thousands in points and fees rolled into the loan.
HOUSING.amber: Fall behind now and it isn't a collection call anymore. It's a foreclosure filing.
HOUSING.blue: The broker is paid on the size of the loan, so he always pushes you to borrow more.
HOUSING.basis: points and fees rolled into a cash-out refinance (2000s dollars)

HOUSING.front: No pay stubs needed. We'll fill in the income for you. (Stated-income loan)
HOUSING.red: The broker writes down an income you don't earn, so you get a payment you can't afford.
HOUSING.amber: The payment is set to that made-up income from month one, and you're behind within the year.
HOUSING.blue: Brokers and lenders were paid more for these loans, and the buyers upstream rarely checked.
HOUSING.basis: a year of a payment set on income you don't earn (2000s dollars)

HOUSING.front: Rates dropped again! Let's refinance and lower your payment.
HOUSING.red: Every refinance charges new points and fees, and each one comes out of your equity.
HOUSING.amber: Each new loan restarts the clock, so the house never gets any closer to paid off.
HOUSING.blue: Brokers flip the same homeowner over and over, because every loan pays them again.
HOUSING.basis: a new round of points and fees with each refinance (2000s dollars)

HOUSING.front: Loan protection included, so your family is covered if something happens to you.
HOUSING.red: One big premium for credit insurance, thousands of dollars, financed into the loan with interest.
HOUSING.amber: It's paid up front for years of coverage; pay the loan off early and little of it comes back.
HOUSING.blue: The lender's own insurance company wrote the policy, and the lender kept the commission.
HOUSING.basis: a single-premium credit insurance policy financed into the loan (2000s dollars)

HOUSING.front: You can always refinance later, once your credit is better.
HOUSING.red: Pay the loan off early and owe a prepayment penalty, often about six months of interest.
HOUSING.amber: The penalty runs two or three years, right through the date the rate resets.
HOUSING.blue: Investors paid more for loans with penalties, so lenders paid brokers more to write them.
HOUSING.basis: six months' interest on a $90,000 loan at 8% (2000s dollars)

HOUSING.front: Behind on the mortgage? Sign the deed over to us and we'll save your house.
HOUSING.red: You hand over the deed and the equity you built, then pay rent to live in your own house.
HOUSING.amber: Miss one rent payment and they evict you; the buyback date comes at a price you can't reach.
HOUSING.blue: The 'rescuer' reads the foreclosure list at the courthouse and knocks on every door on it.
HOUSING.basis: the equity in a paid-down West Side house, signed away (2000s dollars)

HOUSING.front: We'll get your bank to lower your payment. Just $1,500 up front.
HOUSING.red: The fee is gone whether they do anything or not; a HUD-approved counselor does this for free.
HOUSING.amber: They tell you to stop paying the bank while they 'negotiate,' and the sale date gets closer.
HOUSING.blue: Many of these outfits never called the bank at all; they closed up and opened under a new name.
HOUSING.basis: an upfront fee kept whether anything happens (2000s dollars)

HOUSING.front: Notice: your lender has bought insurance on your home for you.
HOUSING.red: It costs several times a regular policy, and it covers the lender's loan, not your things.
HOUSING.amber: The letter gives you a short window to show proof of your own policy; miss it and it's billed to you.
HOUSING.blue: The servicer picks the insurer, and the insurer often pays the servicer back in commissions.
HOUSING.basis: a force-placed policy costing several times a regular one, for a year (2000s dollars)

HOUSING.front: Your broker shops every bank in town to get you the best rate.
HOUSING.red: He put you at a higher rate than you qualified for, and he never said so.
HOUSING.amber: The higher rate costs you every month for as long as you keep the loan.
HOUSING.blue: The lender paid him a bonus for the higher rate. It's called a yield-spread premium.
HOUSING.basis: a rate about one point higher on a $100,000 loan, for a year (2000s dollars)

HOUSING.front: Loans for folks with credit like yours. We specialize in this neighborhood.
HOUSING.red: A subprime rate and fees, even when your credit was good enough for a prime loan.
HOUSING.amber: Your rate resets and your penalty runs, while families across town got fixed rates.
HOUSING.blue: Lenders steered Black neighborhoods to subprime loans, even borrowers who qualified for prime.
HOUSING.basis: a subprime rate instead of prime on an $80,000 loan, for a year (2000s dollars)

HOUSING.front: We were just on your street: new furnace today, financing right at the door.
HOUSING.red: The 'repair' is a high-rate home-equity loan on your house, for work priced far too high.
HOUSING.amber: Payments start whether the work is finished or not, and missing them puts the house at risk.
HOUSING.blue: The contractor brings the lender the loan and gets paid out of it, whatever the work looks like.
HOUSING.basis: an overpriced furnace financed at a high rate against the house (2000s dollars)

HOUSING.front: Free housing counseling: a HUD-approved counselor reads the loan with you.
HOUSING.red: It costs nothing; the counselor doesn't sell loans and goes through every page with you.
HOUSING.amber: Call before you sign, or as soon as you fall behind. Choices shrink as the sale date nears.
HOUSING.blue: Paid for by public grants and nonprofits, not by any lender.
HOUSING.basis: fees and back payments a counselor helps you avoid or work out (2000s dollars)

HOUSING.front: The credit union: refinance into a fixed rate you can actually afford.
HOUSING.red: A fair fixed rate, closing costs spelled out on paper, and no prepayment penalty.
HOUSING.amber: The payment stays the same for the whole loan, with no reset date hiding in the papers.
HOUSING.blue: Member-owned: the profit comes back to the members, not to buyers upstream.
HOUSING.basis: about $300 a month saved against a resetting subprime loan, for a year (2000s dollars)

HOUSING.front: Legal aid will fight the foreclosure with you, for free.
HOUSING.red: No fee if you qualify, and a lawyer checks the loan for every rule it broke.
HOUSING.amber: Answer the foreclosure papers in time: in Ohio you get 28 days after you're served.
HOUSING.blue: Legal aid is funded to defend families, and a loan that broke the law can be fought.
HOUSING.basis: a house kept, and the equity in it (2000s dollars)

LABOR.front: Staffing agency: $9 an hour at the parts plant, start tomorrow.
LABOR.red: The plant pays the agency far more than your $9; the gap is the agency's cut of your work.
LABOR.amber: An assignment ends with one phone call: no notice, no severance, no recall.
LABOR.blue: The plant gets the same work done without the wages, benefits or union contract.
LABOR.basis: the agency's cut of a few dollars an hour, over a year of full-time work (2000s dollars)

LABOR.front: Here's your severance check. Just sign the release first, today.
LABOR.red: Signing gives up your right to sue over the layoff, including age or race discrimination.
LABOR.amber: If you're 40 or older, the law gives you weeks to decide and 7 days to change your mind.
LABOR.blue: The company's lawyers wrote the release to close every claim before anyone looks at it.
LABOR.basis: a severance check, and any claim worth more than it, signed away (2000s dollars)

LABOR.front: Retrain for a new career. Your severance covers the tuition!
LABOR.red: Thousands in tuition and loans for a certificate that local employers don't hire from.
LABOR.amber: The loans come due six months after you finish, job or no job.
LABOR.blue: The school recruits at the union hall the week the plant closes, chasing the severance money.
LABOR.basis: tuition and loans for a certificate that leads nowhere (2000s dollars)

LABOR.front: Keep your 401(k) in company stock. Nobody knows this company like you do.
LABOR.red: Your job and your savings ride on one company; when it fails, you lose both at once.
LABOR.amber: The plan can be frozen during changes, just as the stock is falling.
LABOR.blue: Many companies paid the match in their own stock, which cost them no cash.
LABOR.basis: a 401(k) mostly in company stock when the stock collapses (2000s dollars)

LABOR.front: Work from home: stuff envelopes and earn $500 a week!
LABOR.red: You pay for a 'starter kit,' and there's no real work behind it.
LABOR.amber: Once you've paid, the ads change their name and the phone number stops answering.
LABOR.blue: The only money made is the kit fee, collected from thousands of people who need work.
LABOR.basis: a starter kit for work that doesn't exist (2000s dollars)

LABOR.front: Temp-to-hire: work hard and they'll bring you on full time!
LABOR.red: Temp pay, no benefits, no seniority, for the same work the full-timers do.
LABOR.amber: The hire date keeps moving, month after month, and it never comes.
LABOR.blue: A rotating temp crew costs less than ever hiring anyone for real.
LABOR.basis: a year at temp pay with no benefits instead of a real job (2000s dollars)

LABOR.front: Take the voluntary buyout now. This offer won't be this good again.
LABOR.red: One check, and you give up your seniority, recall rights and retiree health.
LABOR.amber: The window closes in weeks, before anyone knows if the plant is closing anyway.
LABOR.blue: Every worker who takes it is one less the company owes under the contract.
LABOR.basis: seniority, recall rights and retiree health given up for one check (2000s dollars)

LABOR.front: No layoffs are planned. Keep showing up and don't listen to rumors.
LABOR.red: You keep working instead of looking, while the closing may already be planned.
LABOR.amber: The WARN Act requires 60 days' notice of a big layoff; skip it and the company owes back pay.
LABOR.blue: Keeping the news quiet keeps the line running full speed to the last day.
LABOR.basis: about two months of pay and benefits owed when notice is skipped (2000s dollars)

LABOR.front: Your pension is safe for life. Don't worry about the bankruptcy.
LABOR.red: If the plan ends in bankruptcy, the government insurer pays only up to a limit, and checks can shrink.
LABOR.amber: Retirees who organize early can be heard in bankruptcy court; wait, and the deal is done.
LABOR.blue: In bankruptcy, promises to retirees are one more debt the court can cut.
LABOR.basis: a pension check cut down to the insured limit, for a year (2000s dollars)

LABOR.front: The new plant down south is hiring. Move with the company!
LABOR.red: Lower pay, no union, and you pay to move your family away from everyone you know.
LABOR.amber: You have days to decide, and your recall rights here end when you go.
LABOR.blue: The work moved to a non-union plant so the company could pay less; the old wage was the target.
LABOR.basis: lower pay at a non-union plant, plus the cost of the move (2000s dollars)

LABOR.front: Take the concessions and the plant stays open. Sign the new contract.
LABOR.red: Wage and benefit cuts, signed in the hope of saving the plant.
LABOR.amber: The promise to keep the plant open lasts only until the next review.
LABOR.blue: Plants were set against each other to give up the most; the closing list came from the top.
LABOR.basis: a year of wage and benefit cuts given to 'save' the plant (2000s dollars)

LABOR.front: Free retirement seminar for laid-off workers, right here at the hall.
LABOR.red: The 'advice' is to roll your 401(k) into high-fee annuities and funds.
LABOR.amber: Surrender charges lock the money up for years; pull it out early and pay a penalty.
LABOR.blue: The adviser is a salesman paid commissions by the companies whose products he pushes.
LABOR.basis: surrender charges and fees on a rolled-over 401(k) (2000s dollars)

LABOR.front: The union's deal: severance, health coverage, and a job center that places people.
LABOR.red: Severance terms bargained by your union and read by its lawyers before you sign.
LABOR.amber: Sign-up deadlines are real, and the union rep walks you through each one.
LABOR.blue: The union bargained it with the company, and the union answers to you.
LABOR.basis: severance and health coverage bargained by the union (2000s dollars)

LABOR.front: Trade Adjustment Assistance: training and income help if trade cost your job.
LABOR.red: Training paid for, plus weekly income after unemployment runs out, for workers who qualify.
LABOR.amber: Your layoff must be certified and you must start training by a deadline, so sign up fast.
LABOR.blue: A federal program for workers whose jobs went to imports or overseas.
LABOR.basis: a year of paid training and income support (2000s dollars)

LABOR.front: The community college's program, built with a hospital that's hiring.
LABOR.red: Low tuition, often covered by a workforce grant, for a credential the employer asked for.
LABOR.amber: Classes fit around a shift, and the employer interviews graduates as they finish.
LABOR.blue: College, workforce board and employer at one table, answering to the public.
LABOR.basis: tuition covered by a workforce grant (2000s dollars)

options.label: Sell

TODAY.title: Today
TODAY.intro: Good Samaritan Hospital has closed. Gem City Market has opened. The family is still here, and the trap is still here, wearing new clothes.
TODAY.twist: Every History card the family unlocked is in play, and the Elder may teach History twice.
TODAY.face_text: The Ledger Keeper: one hand behind every era. Its hidden hand changes face each round: the store's book (collections), the labor agent (Read −1), the appraiser (+1 Squeeze on your strongest work), the algorithm (an extra strike). It wore The Planter's Ledger, the Labor Agent, the Appraiser, the Council and the Algorithm.

B1_CHAIN.title: The Chain
B1_CHAIN.intro: Marcus can see the second number on everything now, and he teaches it as fast as he can: to Nia, who teaches the next one, who teaches the next.
B1_CHAIN.twist: A Block Party with the Terrell rule. The Chain: when a learner says the second number back, they at once teach one more player in that district, for free.
B1_CHAIN.after: If anyone was burned by the Terrell rule, the ledger reads Terrell. If you won, the block learns Civic Armor: from Chapter 2 on, every Teach comes with cover.

B1_NET.title: The Net
B1_NET.intro: A county job, a desk, a program that sounds like help. The terms keep changing on you.
B1_NET.twist: Full Block with fine-print dice. The Desk: at the start of round 2 one player may take the Desk. At the Desk they gain +1 Trust every round but can't face deals or teach, and every second round its paperwork feeds the Machine an extra strike. Leaving it, for good, takes an action.
B1_NET.face_text: The Net: the program that sounds like help. Relentless: the Machine strikes one extra time every round.
B1_NET.after: If the player at the Desk left it, the ledger reads Quit the desk: in Chapter 3 that player starts with Read 1 everywhere.

B1_CROWN.title: The Crown
B1_CROWN.intro: Somebody offers Dre a way up out of the life, and it looks just like a blessing.
B1_CROWN.twist: Overlord mode, with the stranger's handwriting in place of the Terrell rule. The Crown: once per game the Overlord may offer the Crown to one player. A crowned player can't Fall, but every other block player loses 1 Trust at the start of each round. Refuse it, and the Overlord takes one extra move that round.
B1_CROWN.after: The ledger records whether anyone wore the Crown.

B1_THRONE.title: The Empty Throne
B1_THRONE.intro: No card table to shut down. No leader to arrest. The only way to win is for everybody to read.
B1_THRONE.twist: Full Block with endless deals. No neck for a crown: you can't Expose the Owner until every player has taught at least once, and while any one player holds more than half the table's Props.
B1_THRONE.face_text: The Empty Throne: no face at all, just the system. Relentless: the Machine strikes one extra time every round.
B1_THRONE.after: The book's last scene is on a porch. If you won, read it aloud.

LEDGER.title: The Long Ledger
LEDGER.blurb: One West Dayton family across six generations, from Reconstruction to today.

BOOK_ONE.title: Book One
BOOK_ONE.blurb: Four chapters that follow the novel, from graduation night to the empty throne.

LENDING.front: Tax refund advance: get your ${a} today, no waiting!
LENDING.red: The 'free' advance costs ${c} in filing fees, so you get ${total} of your own ${a} refund.
LENDING.amber: The refund lands in their account first. You wait for them.
LENDING.blue: The tax shop and the bank behind the advance split the fee.

LENDING.front: Quick Cash: borrow ${a} today. One flat fee: just ${c}.
LENDING.red: A ${c} fee on ${a} for {b} days is a {total}% yearly rate. The fee is the product.
LENDING.amber: Due in full in {b} days. Can't pay? Roll it over and owe ${c} again.
LENDING.blue: The storefront and the debt buyer that calls you later share one owner.
LENDING.ask: A ${c} fee on ${a} for {b} days. As a yearly rate: ${c} ÷ ${a} × 365 ÷ {b} = ?

LENDING.front: Borrow ${s} today. Low monthly payments of just ${a}!
LENDING.red: ${a} × {b} months = ${total}. That's ${over} more than you borrowed.
LENDING.amber: Miss one payment and a 'late plan' you never asked for gets added to the loan.
LENDING.blue: The loan is sold to a debt buyer before the ink dries.

LENDING.front: Title loan: ${s} cash on your car title, and you keep driving.
LENDING.red: ${a} × {b} months = ${total} to borrow ${s}: ${over} extra.
LENDING.amber: One missed payment and the car is gone, often with no grace period.
LENDING.blue: The lender owns a piece of the repo lot that resells your car.

LENDING.front: Credit union starter loan: ${a} a month for {b} months.
LENDING.red: ${a} × {b} = ${total} in all, at a low fixed rate with no fees. This one's honest.
LENDING.amber: No rollover, no balloon payment, and paying early costs nothing.
LENDING.blue: Owned by its members, the people on the block who save there.

HOUSING.front: First month free! Then just ${a} a month, {b}-month lease.
HOUSING.red: ${a} × {b} = ${ab}, plus ${c} in 'amenity' and admin fees: ${total}, and the free month is spread over the rest.
HOUSING.amber: Break the lease early and the free month gets billed back to you.
HOUSING.blue: The amenity fee goes to the management company, not the building.

HOUSING.front: Rent-to-own: a brand-new {item} for just ${a} a week!
HOUSING.red: ${a} × {b} weeks = ${total} for a {item} the store sells for ${s}.
HOUSING.amber: Miss a week and they can pick it up, along with everything you've paid.
HOUSING.blue: The same company runs the store, the financing, and the collections.

HOUSING.front: Own this house in Madden Hills: ${c} down, ${a} a month, no bank needed.
HOUSING.red: ${c} down + ${a} × {b} months = ${total}, for a house appraised at ${s}.
HOUSING.amber: Miss one payment and you lose the house and everything you paid in: no deed until the last check.
HOUSING.blue: The seller bought it at a tax sale for almost nothing and has sold it this way before.

HOUSING.front: Apartments on Salem Avenue: apply today, just ${a} an application!
HOUSING.red: {b} applications × ${a} = ${total}, and most never call you back.
HOUSING.amber: The fee is gone the moment you hit submit, approved or not.
HOUSING.blue: The 'screening company' belongs to the landlord's management firm.

HOUSING.front: Homeownership program: ${a} a month for {b} months toward a house with a real deed.
HOUSING.red: ${a} × {b} = ${total}, and every dollar of it builds equity. This one's honest.
HOUSING.amber: A missed month gets a counselor's call, not an eviction.
HOUSING.blue: A neighborhood land trust, run by the people who live here.

LABOR.front: Delivery app: make ${a} a trip, choose your own hours!
LABOR.red: {b} trips × ${a} = ${ab}, minus ${c} in gas and wear on your car: ${total} for the day.
LABOR.amber: The pay per trip can change any week, without notice.
LABOR.blue: The app counts you as a contractor so it pays nothing toward your car or your health.

LABOR.front: Warehouse work through the agency: ${a} an hour, start Monday!
LABOR.red: {b} hours × ${a} = ${ab}, minus a ${c} weekly 'van fee' = ${total} a week.
LABOR.amber: The agency can end the job any day, and the 90-day hire-on keeps moving.
LABOR.blue: The plant pays the agency almost twice what reaches you.

LABOR.front: Sign-on bonus: ${s} cash when you start!
LABOR.red: Leave before {b} months and you pay back the ${s} plus ${c} in 'training': ${total}.
LABOR.amber: The {b}-month clock restarts if they move you to another shift.
LABOR.blue: The same staffing firm writes the payback loan and sues to collect it.

LABOR.front: Security job, ${a} an hour, uniform included!
LABOR.red: "Included" means ${c} a week out of your check for {b} weeks: ${total}. (The math: ${c} × {b}.)
LABOR.amber: Quit early and the rest of the uniform cost comes out of your last check.
LABOR.blue: The uniform company is owned by the guard firm's parent company.

LABOR.front: Union apprenticeship: ${a} an hour while you learn, a raise every {b} months.
LABOR.red: {c} hours × ${a} = ${total} a week, with no fees taken out. This one's honest.
LABOR.amber: The raises are in the contract: on the date, every time.
LABOR.blue: The hall is run by the members, the people doing the work.

HEALTH.front: Teeth whitening kit: just ${a} a month, cancel anytime!
HEALTH.red: ${a} × {b} months = ${total} a year. 'Cancel anytime' means calling during business hours.
HEALTH.amber: The free trial turns into a monthly charge in 7 days.
HEALTH.blue: The same company sells the 'dentist-approved' reviews.

HEALTH.front: Get the dental work today: 0% interest for {b} months on the clinic card!
HEALTH.red: Owe even $1 on day {b} and all the interest lands at once: ${c}, for ${total} in all.
HEALTH.amber: The 0% clock runs {b} months. One late payment ends it early.
HEALTH.blue: The card company pays the clinic to sign patients up in the chair.

HEALTH.front: Health plan: just ${a} a month!
HEALTH.red: ${a} × {b} = ${ab} a year, and you pay the first ${c} yourself: ${total} before it pays a dime.
HEALTH.amber: Sign-up closes Friday. After that you wait a year.
HEALTH.blue: The 'plan' is a discount card sold by the same company that runs the ads.

HEALTH.front: Settle that ER bill: just ${a} a month for {b} months.
HEALTH.red: ${a} × {b} = ${total}, ${over} more than the bill itself.
HEALTH.amber: You have 240 days from the first bill to apply for help. The clock already started.
HEALTH.blue: The hospital is a nonprofit that owes charity care: you might owe nothing at all.

HEALTH.front: Community health center: a sliding-scale visit, ${a} today.
HEALTH.red: {b} visits × ${a} = ${total} for the year. No surprise bill. This one's honest.
HEALTH.amber: No deadline: they see you whether or not you can pay today.
HEALTH.blue: Run by a board that's mostly patients, the way the law requires.

EDUCATION.front: Private student loan: ${s}, just ${a} a month after you graduate!
EDUCATION.red: ${a} × {b} months = ${total} to borrow ${s}: ${over} extra.
EDUCATION.amber: Interest piles up the whole time you're in school, before the first payment.
EDUCATION.blue: The lender pays the school to be on its 'preferred' list.

EDUCATION.front: Career college: certified in {b} months, just ${a} a month!
EDUCATION.red: ${a} × {b} = ${total}. The same certificate at Sinclair runs about ${s}.
EDUCATION.amber: Drop after week 3 and you owe the whole term.
EDUCATION.blue: The school's owners also own the lender in the financial aid office.

EDUCATION.front: Test-prep: ${a} a session, a higher score guaranteed!
EDUCATION.red: {b} sessions × ${a} = ${total}, and the guarantee is only a free retake.
EDUCATION.amber: Cancel within 3 days or you're billed for every session.
EDUCATION.blue: The free practice test at the library is the same one.

EDUCATION.front: A school laptop for ${a} a week. No credit check!
EDUCATION.red: ${a} × {b} weeks = ${total} for a ${s} laptop: ${over} extra.
EDUCATION.amber: Miss a week and the laptop locks itself.
EDUCATION.blue: The lender pays the school for the flyer in your kid's backpack.

EDUCATION.front: College aid night at Dunbar: fill out the FAFSA with a counselor. {b} grants to try for.
EDUCATION.red: It costs ${total}. Grants don't get paid back. This one's honest.
EDUCATION.amber: The state deadline is real: go early.
EDUCATION.blue: Run by the school and Central State volunteers.
EDUCATION.ask: What does filling out the FAFSA cost? ${a} × {b} = ?

LENDING.front: Neighborhood credit union loan: fixed low rate, no fees.
LENDING.red: A fair, fixed rate, and no fees to sign.
LENDING.amber: No deadline: take your time and read it at home.
LENDING.blue: COUNTERFEIT. A storefront lender using a look-alike name; the real rate is in a second agreement.
LENDING.basis: a high-cost loan dressed as a credit union

HOUSING.front: A fair lease: normal deposit, clear terms.
HOUSING.red: Rent is the rent; the deposit is refundable.
HOUSING.amber: Standard 30-day notice on both sides.
HOUSING.blue: COUNTERFEIT. The landlord is a shell company with dozens of eviction filings; a fee addendum is stapled behind page 4.
HOUSING.basis: a fee addendum and a deposit that never comes back

LABOR.front: Union-scale job: overtime and benefits from day one.
LABOR.red: Overtime, benefits, and the employer pays its share of taxes.
LABOR.amber: Your first check comes in two weeks.
LABOR.blue: COUNTERFEIT. A staffing agency borrowed the union's name; page 6 makes you a contractor with no overtime.
LABOR.basis: overtime and benefits that were never in the contract

HEALTH.front: The hospital's financial-help program: apply right here.
HEALTH.red: Your bill could drop to a fraction, or to nothing.
HEALTH.amber: Apply within 240 days of your first bill.
HEALTH.blue: COUNTERFEIT. A medical-credit company dressed as the hospital's charity program; deferred interest applies.
HEALTH.basis: deferred interest where charity care should have been

EDUCATION.front: Free help with your federal student loans.
EDUCATION.red: Federal repayment and forgiveness programs, filed for you.
EDUCATION.amber: Sign up before the program deadline.
EDUCATION.blue: COUNTERFEIT. A 'document prep' company charging for free federal forms, and keeping your login.
EDUCATION.basis: fees for free federal forms, and your account login
